title: Rate policy unit mismatch after rate-limiter migration causes cross-environment 429s
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Multiple high-volume customers (hosted, Dedicated pools, and Private VPC agents) observed opaque 429s during a cross-region capacity failover. Support escalations reported sudden sustained throttles despite quota headroom. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigation, and a targeted fix for a rate policy translation mismatch introduced during the recent rate-limiter migration (legacy -> rl-v2 serialization).
impact_summary: Intermittent but sustained 429s across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private environments for several large tenants over a ~3 hour window. Some customers saw throughput drop by ~90% and experienced production user-facing errors. Mobile app teams reported elevated error rates and increased latency as clients retried. Incident severity escalated to P0.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy new rate-limiter control-plane policy with unit=PER_MINUTE encoded as rl-v2 protobuf; 2) Trigger config sync to Private agents (agent v1.8) or Dedicated pool proxies; 3) Simulate steady client load that previously fit within quota; 4) Observe 429s immediately after sync. Note: reproduction requires agent with older enum handling (agent v1.8 or earlier).
timeline: 2026-02-27 03:40 UTC - first customer report via SRE Slack; 2026-02-27 04:10 UTC - elevated 429s across multiple tenants; 2026-02-27 04:45 UTC - priority incident declared; 2026-02-27 05:30 UTC - rollback of config to pre-migration policies reduced errors for Hosted; 2026-02-27 08:10 UTC - hotfix for Private agent released to a small canary; 2026-02-27 10:00 UTC - full Private/Dedicated rollout completed with monitoring and throttling metrics stabilized; ongoing: postmortem and long-term fixes scheduled.
investigation_findings: The rl-v2 protobuf added an explicit "unit" enum (PER_SECOND | PER_MINUTE | PER_HOUR) replacing the legacy implicit 'per minute' assumption. Agent v1.8 (private/on-prem customers and older dedicated proxies) did not recognize the new enum numeric values and defaulted to interpreting the unit field as 0 (== PER_SECOND). As a result, policies encoded as PER_MINUTE were enforced as PER_SECOND on those agents, reducing allowed tokens by ~60x and producing opaque 429s. Hosted control-plane and newer agents (v1.9+) decode correctly, which explains mixed customer impact during a staged rollout.
root_cause: Serialization/enumeration compatibility bug introduced during rate-limiter migration: control plane started emitting rl-v2 proto enums whose numeric values differ from the legacy representation. Backward-incompatible enum mapping in older agents led to misinterpreted rate units (minute->second), causing effective quota reduction and customer outages.
immediate_mitigation: 1) Reverted to legacy-encoded rate policies for Private and Dedicated clusters while rollback ensured zero-downtime for hosted customers; 2) Deployed agent v1.8-hotfix that explicitly handles both legacy and rl-v2 enums (compatibility branch) to the highest-risk Private customers; 3) Opened support-driven temporary bypass to ignore the unit field for critical tenants as stop-gap; 4) Added a fast circuit in the control plane to block rl-v2 policy pushes to agents reporting versions <1.9.
long_term_fix: 1) Release agent v1.10 with formal backward compatibility and unit tests that validate enum mappings; 2) Add an automated compatibility check to the control plane that rejects rl-v2 policy pushes to clusters with incompatible agent versions; 3) Add a pre-deploy conversion step in the policy compiler that includes explicit unit normalization metadata; 4) Update rollout playbook to include compatibility matrix verification for any proto changes.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (hotfix): deploy agent v1.8-hotfix to canary Private customers (completed); Phase 2 (patch): publish agent v1.10 and force-upgrade Dedicated proxies during a maintenance window; Phase 3 (safety): update control plane policy compiler and enable compatibility gate for rl-v2; Phase 4: run full canary across Hosted, then lift compatibility gate and adopt rl-v2. Target completion: runtime-1.19.2-hotfix by 2026-03-20.
test_plan: Unit tests for proto enum mappings; integration tests simulating control-plane -> agent policy sync with agents reporting versions 1.7-1.10; load tests exercising quotas at per-second and per-minute scales; regression tests added to CI that validate no silent unit demotion occurs; post-deploy smoke checks for 429 rate across representative tenants.
